description: The only comment bodies the triage agent may post. Adapted from pytorch/pytorch .agents/skills/triaging-issues/templates.json (BSD-3-Clause). Differences from upstream: no template closes an issue and no template edits the issue body; a maintainer does both if needed. The agent posts at most ONE comment per run, so when several templates apply, join their bodies in the order listed in SKILL.md under a single header and footer.
header:
> [!NOTE]
> Automated first-pass triage (AI-generated, not yet reviewed by a maintainer). Labels and suggestions may be wrong; a maintainer will confirm.

redirect_to_forum.use_when: The issue is a usage or process question, not a bug report or feature request.
redirect_to_forum.body: This looks like a usage question rather than a bug report or feature request. Usage questions get faster answers on the [PyTorch Discussion Forum](https://discuss.pytorch.org/), where both the community and maintainers respond. A maintainer will decide whether to close this issue; if you believe it is actually a bug, please add a minimal reproduction.

request_more_info.use_when: There is not enough information to tell whether this is a bug, a feature request or a question, or the report has no reproduction at all.
request_more_info.body:
Thanks for the report. To triage this, could you share:

- A minimal repro (a small, self-contained script or exact steps)
- The full error message / stack trace
- The output of `python -m torch.utils.collect_env`

request_self_contained_reproduction.use_when: Reproducing the issue requires downloading external files (.zip, .pt, .pth, .pkl, .safetensors, .onnx, .bin) or files from external storage (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Mega, WeTransfer, Hugging Face model files).
request_self_contained_reproduction.body: Maintainers avoid downloading external files to reproduce issues. Could you reproduce this with a self-contained script instead (for example with random weights or synthetic data)? If the files contain extreme values (very large values, NaN, inf), please mention that too.

possible_duplicate.use_when: You read a find_duplicates.py review candidate and confirmed it describes the same defect (same component, symptom and trigger).
possible_duplicate.body: This may be a duplicate of #{number} ("{title}"). If it is the same problem, please follow that issue instead; if not, please explain the difference so a maintainer can keep both open.

numerical_accuracy.use_when: You applied 'module: edge cases' because the report is about extremal values or precision differences between backends/dtypes.
numerical_accuracy.body: This may be related to expected floating-point accuracy limits. PyTorch documents behaviour for extremal values and backend/dtype precision differences in the [Numerical Accuracy notes](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/numerical_accuracy.html). If you believe this goes beyond expected numerical behaviour, a reproducer with values well inside the normal range would help.
